notes: Free in restaurants: ask for お水 (omizu). Tap water is safe to drink everywhere.

examples.tl: お水をください。
examples.rom: Omizu o kudasai.
examples.en: Water, please.

notes: Usually green tea, often free with meals. 紅茶 (kōcha) = black tea, 麦茶 (mugicha) = barley tea.

examples.tl: 温かいお茶をお願いします。
examples.rom: Atatakai ocha o onegai shimasu.
examples.en: Hot tea, please.

notes: ブラック = black, ミルク = milk, 砂糖 (satō) = sugar. Convenience-store coffee is good and cheap.

examples.tl: アイスコーヒーを一つください。
examples.rom: Aisu kōhī o hitotsu kudasai.
examples.en: One iced coffee, please.

notes: Long ī: ビル (biru) with a short i means 'building'. 瓶ビール (bin bīru) = bottled beer.

examples.tl: ビールを二本ください。
examples.rom: Bīru o nihon kudasai.
examples.en: Two bottles of beer, please.

notes: Usually ordered as just 生 (nama). 中 (chū) is the standard medium mug.

examples.tl: とりあえず生を二つください。
examples.rom: Toriaezu nama o futatsu kudasai.
examples.en: Two draft beers to start, please.

notes: What English calls sake. 冷酒 (reishu) = chilled, 冷や (hiya) = room temperature, 熱燗 (atsukan) = hot.

examples.tl: おすすめの日本酒はありますか。
examples.rom: Osusume no nihonshu wa arimasu ka.
examples.en: Do you have a sake you recommend?

notes: Any alcoholic drink, not only sake. The legal drinking age is 20.

examples.tl: 今日はお酒を飲みません。
examples.rom: Kyō wa osake o nomimasen.
examples.en: I'm not drinking alcohol today.

notes: Cooked rice, and by extension a meal. Western-style menus say ライス (raisu).

examples.tl: ご飯は大盛りでお願いします。
examples.rom: Gohan wa ōmori de onegai shimasu.
examples.en: A large serving of rice, please.

notes: お肉 (oniku) is the softer everyday form.

examples.tl: これは何の肉ですか。
examples.rom: Kore wa nan no niku desu ka.
examples.en: What kind of meat is this?

notes: On menus often just 牛 (gyū): 牛丼 (gyūdon) = beef bowl, 和牛 (wagyū) = Japanese beef.

examples.tl: 牛肉は食べません。
examples.rom: Gyūniku wa tabemasen.
examples.en: I don't eat beef.

notes: On menus 豚 is read buta or ton: とんかつ (tonkatsu) = pork cutlet. Ramen broth is often pork.

examples.tl: このスープに豚肉は入っていますか。
examples.rom: Kono sūpu ni butaniku wa haitte imasu ka.
examples.en: Is there pork in this soup?

notes: Menus also write とり or 鳥. 唐揚げ (karaage) = fried chicken.

examples.tl: 鶏肉の定食をお願いします。
examples.rom: Toriniku no teishoku o onegai shimasu.
examples.en: The chicken set meal, please.

notes: 刺身 (sashimi) = sliced raw fish; 焼き魚 (yakizakana) = grilled fish.

examples.tl: 今日の魚は何ですか。
examples.rom: Kyō no sakana wa nan desu ka.
examples.en: What is today's fish?

notes: サラダ (sarada) = salad. Restaurant meals are light on vegetables; convenience stores sell salads.

examples.tl: 野菜の料理はありますか。
examples.rom: Yasai no ryōri wa arimasu ka.
examples.en: Do you have vegetable dishes?

notes: Styles: 醤油 (shōyu) soy, 味噌 (miso), 塩 (shio) salt, 豚骨 (tonkotsu) pork bone. Slurping is fine.

examples.tl: 味噌ラーメンを一つください。
examples.rom: Miso rāmen o hitotsu kudasai.
examples.en: One miso ramen, please.

notes: 回転寿司 (kaitenzushi) = conveyor-belt sushi: cheap, easy, ordered by tablet.

examples.tl: 近くにおいしい寿司屋はありますか。
examples.rom: Chikaku ni oishii sushiya wa arimasu ka.
examples.en: Is there a good sushi restaurant nearby?

notes: Hot in broth, or cold with a dipping sauce (ざるそば zarusoba). Nikko is known for it.

examples.tl: 冷たいそばをお願いします。
examples.rom: Tsumetai soba o onegai shimasu.
examples.en: Cold soba, please.

notes: Thick, white and chewy; hot or cold. Cheap standing shops are found in stations.

examples.tl: 天ぷらうどんを一つください。
examples.rom: Tenpura udon o hitotsu kudasai.
examples.en: One tempura udon, please.

notes: A main dish with rice, miso soup and pickles: the best-value lunch.

examples.tl: 焼き魚定食をお願いします。
examples.rom: Yakizakana teishoku o onegai shimasu.
examples.en: The grilled fish set meal, please.

notes: Choose たれ (tare) sauce or 塩 (shio) salt. Counted with 本: 二本 = two skewers.

examples.tl: 焼き鳥を五本、塩でお願いします。
examples.rom: Yakitori o gohon, shio de onegai shimasu.
examples.en: Five chicken skewers with salt, please.

notes: The convenience-store staple. Fillings: 鮭 (sake) salmon, 梅 (ume) pickled plum, ツナマヨ tuna mayo.

examples.tl: 山でおにぎりを食べます。
examples.rom: Yama de onigiri o tabemasu.
examples.en: I'll eat rice balls on the mountain.

notes: 駅弁 (ekiben) = station bento. Eating on a Shinkansen or limited express is normal; on commuter trains it is not.

examples.tl: 駅でお弁当を買いましょう。
examples.rom: Eki de obentō o kaimashō.
examples.en: Let's buy a bento at the station.

notes: Nikko's specialty, served rolled, as sashimi or on soba. In Nikko it is written 湯波.

examples.tl: 日光で湯葉そばを食べました。
examples.rom: Nikkō de yuba soba o tabemashita.
examples.en: I had yuba soba in Nikko.

notes: Many places use a tablet or a QR code. Photo menus make pointing easy.

examples.tl: メニューをお願いします。
examples.rom: Menyū o onegai shimasu.
examples.en: The menu, please.

notes: ご注文は？ (gochūmon wa?) = what would you like? Tables often have a call button (呼び出しボタン).

examples.tl: 注文してもいいですか。
examples.rom: Chūmon shite mo ii desu ka.
examples.en: May I order?

notes: Menus mark it おすすめ or 人気 (ninki, popular).

examples.tl: おすすめは何ですか。
examples.rom: Osusume wa nan desu ka.
examples.en: What do you recommend?

examples.tl: このラーメンはおいしいです。
examples.rom: Kono rāmen wa oishii desu.
examples.en: This ramen is delicious.

notes: 辛口 (karakuchi) on a curry label = hot; on sake = dry. 甘い (amai) = sweet.

examples.tl: これは辛いですか。
examples.rom: Kore wa karai desu ka.
examples.en: Is this spicy?

notes: For drinks the choice is アイス or ホット (hotto). On its own アイス can also mean ice cream.

examples.tl: 「ホットですか、アイスですか。」「アイスでお願いします。」
examples.rom: Hotto desu ka, aisu desu ka. / Aisu de onegai shimasu.
examples.en: Hot or iced? / Iced, please.

notes: Never stand them upright in rice or pass food chopstick to chopstick: both are funeral customs.

examples.tl: お箸をもう一つもらえますか。
examples.rom: Ohashi o mō hitotsu moraemasu ka.
examples.en: Could I have another pair of chopsticks?

notes: Mostly for Western-style places. Japanese ones are 〜屋 (-ya): ラーメン屋, 寿司屋, そば屋.

examples.tl: ホテルにレストランはありますか。
examples.rom: Hoteru ni resutoran wa arimasu ka.
examples.en: Is there a restaurant in the hotel?

notes: Drinks plus small shared dishes. Expect a small table charge (お通し).

examples.tl: 今晩、居酒屋に行きませんか。
examples.rom: Konban, izakaya ni ikimasen ka.
examples.en: Shall we go to an izakaya tonight?

notes: 7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart: food, ATMs, toilets and tickets, mostly open 24 hours.

examples.tl: コンビニで朝ご飯を買います。
examples.rom: Konbini de asagohan o kaimasu.
examples.en: I'll buy breakfast at the convenience store.

notes: At ramen and beef-bowl shops you buy it from the machine by the door, then hand it to the staff.

examples.tl: 先に食券を買ってください。
examples.rom: Saki ni shokken o katte kudasai.
examples.en: Please buy a meal ticket first.

notes: A fixed price for about 90 to 120 minutes. 食べ放題 (tabehōdai) = all-you-can-eat.

examples.tl: 飲み放題はいくらですか。
examples.rom: Nomihōdai wa ikura desu ka.
examples.en: How much is all-you-can-drink?

notes: The small dish you didn't order at an izakaya. It is the cover charge (a few hundred yen), not a scam.

examples.tl: 「これは頼んでいません。」「お通しです。」
examples.rom: Kore wa tanonde imasen. / Otōshi desu.
examples.en: I didn't order this. / It's the table-charge appetizer.

notes: Thing + アレルギーがあります. 卵 tamago egg, 小麦 komugi wheat, えび ebi shrimp, ナッツ nattsu nuts.

examples.tl: 私はえびアレルギーがあります。
examples.rom: Watashi wa ebi arerugī ga arimasu.
examples.en: I have a shrimp allergy.

notes: Plain form: 食べる (taberu). 食べられません (taberaremasen) = I can't eat it.

examples.tl: 何でも食べます。
examples.rom: Nan demo tabemasu.
examples.en: I eat anything.

notes: Plain form: 飲む (nomu). Also used for taking medicine: 薬を飲みます.

examples.tl: 何を飲みますか。
examples.rom: Nani o nomimasu ka.
examples.en: What will you have to drink?

notes: Staff ask 店内ですか、お持ち帰りですか: eat in or take out?

examples.tl: 持ち帰りでお願いします。
examples.rom: Mochikaeri de onegai shimasu.
examples.en: To go, please.

notes: Not widely understood: say exactly what you can't eat. Fish stock (だし) is in most soups and sauces.

examples.tl: 私はベジタリアンです。肉と魚は食べません。
examples.rom: Watashi wa bejitarian desu. Niku to sakana wa tabemasen.
examples.en: I'm vegetarian. I don't eat meat or fish.

notes: Usually made from bonito flakes and kelp, so 'vegetable' dishes often still contain fish.

examples.tl: このだしに魚は入っていますか。
examples.rom: Kono dashi ni sakana wa haitte imasu ka.
examples.en: Is there fish in this stock?

notes: Everywhere. Red label あたたかい = hot, blue つめたい = cold. Many take Suica.

examples.tl: 自動販売機で水を買います。
examples.rom: Jidōhanbaiki de mizu o kaimasu.
examples.en: I'll buy water from the vending machine.

notes: Called about 30 minutes before closing. In small towns like Nikko, kitchens can close by 8 pm.

examples.tl: ラストオーダーは何時ですか。
examples.rom: Rasuto ōdā wa nanji desu ka.
examples.en: What time is last order?

notes: The answer to 店内でお召し上がりですか. Tax is 10% eating in and 8% for takeout.

examples.tl: 「店内でお召し上がりですか。」「はい、店内で。」
examples.rom: Tennai de omeshiagari desu ka. / Hai, tennai de.
examples.en: Will you be eating in? / Yes, for here.

accept: Would you like it warmed up?
notes: Asked at convenience stores when you buy a bento. Answer はい、お願いします or 大丈夫です.

examples.tl: 「お弁当、温めますか。」「はい、お願いします。」
examples.rom: Obentō, atatamemasu ka. / Hai, onegai shimasu.
examples.en: Shall I heat up your bento? / Yes, please.

tl: お会計をお願いします。
accept_tl: お勘定をお願いします
notes: Often you take the slip from your table to the register by the door. No tipping.

examples.tl: すみません、お会計をお願いします。カードで。
examples.rom: Sumimasen, okaikei o onegai shimasu. Kādo de.
examples.en: Excuse me, the bill, please. By card.

tl: 英語のメニューはありますか。
rom: Eigo no menyū wa arimasu ka.
en: Do you have an English menu?
accept: Do you have a menu in English?

examples.tl: 「英語のメニューはありますか。」「はい、少々お待ちください。」
examples.rom: Eigo no menyū wa arimasu ka. / Hai, shōshō omachi kudasai.
examples.en: Do you have an English menu? / Yes, one moment, please.

notes: Said by everyone before eating, often with hands together. Literally 'I receive'.

examples.tl: おいしそうですね。いただきます。
examples.rom: Oishisō desu ne. Itadakimasu.
examples.en: That looks delicious. Let's eat.

notes: Said after eating, and to the staff as you leave a restaurant.

examples.tl: ごちそうさまでした。おいしかったです。
examples.rom: Gochisōsama deshita. Oishikatta desu.
examples.en: Thank you for the meal. It was delicious.

notes: Thing + は食べられません. Staff take 'can't' more seriously than 'don't like'.

examples.tl: 生の魚は食べられません。
examples.rom: Nama no sakana wa taberaremasen.
examples.en: I can't eat raw fish.

accept: Does this have meat in it?
notes: Thing + は入っていますか = is there any ... in it?

examples.tl: これにナッツは入っていますか。
examples.rom: Kore ni nattsu wa haitte imasu ka.
examples.en: Are there nuts in this?

tl: わさび抜きでお願いします。
notes: Thing + 抜きで (nuki de) = without it: 肉抜き, ネギ抜き (no green onion), 氷抜き (no ice).

examples.tl: アイスコーヒーを氷抜きでお願いします。
examples.rom: Aisu kōhī o kōri nuki de onegai shimasu.
examples.en: An iced coffee with no ice, please.

notes: 一緒で (issho de) = all together. Some small places take only one payment per table.

examples.tl: 「お会計はご一緒ですか。」「別々でお願いします。」
examples.rom: Okaikei wa goissho desu ka. / Betsubetsu de onegai shimasu.
examples.en: Are you paying together? / Separately, please.

tl: ビールをもう一杯ください。
accept: One more glass of beer, please
notes: 杯 (hai) counts glasses and bowls: ippai, nihai, sanbai. おかわり (okawari) = a refill.

examples.tl: お水をもう一杯もらえますか。
examples.rom: Omizu o mō ippai moraemasu ka.
examples.en: Could I have another glass of water?

notes: Past of おいしい. Saying it to the cook on the way out is always welcome.

examples.tl: とてもおいしかったです。また来ます。
examples.rom: Totemo oishikatta desu. Mata kimasu.
examples.en: It was very delicious. I'll come again.
